records.central_claim: Ulama is a living set of Sinaloan rubber-ball game variants with documented pre-Columbian roots; scholarship describes it as a modern surviving form of the Mesoamerican ballgame. The broader Mesoamerican ballgame tradition is approximately 3,500 years old, while the earliest currently documented formal ballcourt dates to about 1650 BCE. Spanish colonial suppression and survival in limited Sinaloan communities are documented, but the evidence does not establish an unchanged single sport called ulama played continuously for exactly 3,400 years or a general late-20th-century rebirth.
